html:
Luoyang is a city on the Luo river near the Yellow River in Henan, central China, and one of the country's great ancient capitals. More than a dozen dynasties ruled from it over some 1,500 years.

The area is one of the cradles of Chinese civilisation; the early Bronze Age site of Erlitou lies nearby. The Zhou built a second capital here, and from 771 BCE it was their only one, in the Eastern Zhou period.

The Eastern Han made Luoyang their capital from 25 CE. It became the main eastern end of the Silk Road and the place where Buddhism reached China: the White Horse Temple, by tradition China's first Buddhist temple, was founded there in the first century. The scholar Zhang Heng worked at the Han court in Luoyang. The city was burned in 190 at the end of the Han, and again in 311, when Xiongnu forces sacked it; the Sogdian Ancient Letters report that disaster.

The Northern Wei moved their capital there in 494 and began carving the Longmen Grottoes nearby. Under the Sui and Tang it was the eastern capital, and Empress Wu Zetian preferred it to Chang'an. After the Tang, power moved east and north, and Luoyang became a provincial city, famous for its peonies.
sum: Luoyang is a city on the Luo river near the Yellow River in Henan, central China, and one of the country's great ancient capitals. More than a dozen dynasties ruled from it over some 1,500 years.
